title: Morning and evening
hook: the prayer book's two daily offices, morning prayer and evening prayer

segments.voice: Yesterday, peregrinatio: Irish Christians pushing off in boats with no oars. Your line was where the wind takes. Where did an unplanned turn lead you? Day one thousand one hundred fifty-three.

"Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud: and he shall hear my voice." That's Psalm fifty-five, someone in real trouble, hanging their prayers on the clock. The rhythm turns up elsewhere too. In Exodus, one lamb is offered in the morning and another at evening, day by day. The day has two hinges: getting up and lying down. The Church of England's Book of Common Prayer built on those hinges. It heads its two daily services The Order for Morning Prayer and The Order for Evening Prayer, each one daily throughout the year. Today the Anglican way of prayer begins, with a door at each end of the day.
screen: `ONE LAMB AT MORNING, ONE AT EVENING.`

segments.voice: Open the old prayer book and the shape is plain. Morning Prayer opens with lines of scripture and a confession said together, and soon after comes a short exchange. The minister says, "O Lord, open thou our lips." The people answer, "And our mouth shall shew forth thy praise." Then come psalms, a reading from the Old Testament, a song, a reading from the New Testament, another song, the creed, the Lord's Prayer, and short prayers called collects. Evening Prayer has the same bones, with its own songs and its own collects. The book even lays out the psalms so that, morning and evening, the whole Psalter is read through each month. Now look at the last collect on each side of the day. In the morning: "O Lord, our heavenly Father, Almighty and everlasting God, who hast safely brought us to the beginning of this day." At night: "Lighten our darkness, we beseech thee, O Lord; and by thy great mercy defend us from all perils and dangers of this night." One prayer stands at the door of the morning and says thank you for getting here. The other stands at the door of the dark and asks for keeping. Tradition says Thomas Cranmer, the archbishop who shaped the English prayer book, folded the monastery's many hours of prayer into these two, so a farmer or a shopkeeper could keep them as well as a monk. Psalm ninety-two already had the idea: "To shew forth thy lovingkindness in the morning, and thy faithfulness every night." Love at the start. Faithfulness at the close. Some Anglicans pray the full offices in church. Some say them at a kitchen table. Some keep only the collects. The length can change. The two hinges stay.
screen: `BROUGHT TO THE BEGINNING OF THIS DAY.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray one office, or one small piece of one. Whichever end of the day you're at, sit up and let your breath slow down. If it's morning, take the old opening line: O Lord, open thou our lips. If it's evening, take the night one: lighten our darkness. If you pray, let the line be your prayer for a while. If you don't, simply hold it, and notice the hinge of the day turning: the hours behind you, the hours ahead. The bell holds the time.
Morning and evening. The prayer book's two daily offices, Morning Prayer and Evening Prayer: the two hinges of the day, both turned toward God.
Your line: morning and evening. Today, mark both ends: one line when you get up, one line before you sleep. The same line both times is fine. Day one thousand one hundred fifty-three.

howItsDone: In the Anglican tradition, Morning and Evening Prayer from the Book of Common Prayer or a newer prayer book are said or sung daily in some cathedrals and parishes, and some clergy and lay people pray them on their own at home.

notes: The index hook says 'prayed by millions'; the number is cut under the claims rule, and the file's hook line is reworded accordingly. The index itself is unchanged.

'Its title page promises an order for Morning Prayer and Evening Prayer, daily, throughout the year': the 1662 title page lists 'Morning and Evening Prayer'; the service headings read 'The Order for Morning Prayer, Daily Throughout the Year'. Confirm the wording is fair.

Order of Morning Prayer (sentences, exhortation, general confession, absolution, Lord's Prayer, versicles, psalms, two lessons each followed by a canticle, Creed, Lord's Prayer, suffrages, collects) summarized; confirm. The summary skips the opening sentences and exhortation.
'The whole Psalter is read through each month' comes from the 1662 rubric 'The Psalter shall be read through once every Month'. Confirm.
'Tradition says Thomas Cranmer ... folded the monastery's many hours of prayer into these two' is a standard historical account, attributed to tradition; confirm.
Fork reveal says 'a line from Psalm 51' (51:15 KJV: 'O Lord, open thou my lips; and my mouth shall shew forth thy praise'); the prayer book uses 'our'. Confirm.
Original: עֶרֶב וָבֹקֶר appears in Psalm 55:18 in the Hebrew numbering (55:17 in English). Check vocalization and pronunciation.
